study_design: Hospital-based case-control study conducted in Italy between 1991 and 2002, with incident prostate cancer cases, BPH cases, and hospital controls.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: A total of 2663 men younger than 75 years had incident, histologically confirmed prostate carcinoma (1294 cases) or symptomatic obstructive BPH (1369 cases) (maximal flow rate less than 15 mL/s) refractory to medical treatment. A total of 1451 patients younger than 75 years were used as controls.
reason: The abstract analyzes incident, histologically confirmed prostate carcinoma overall. It does not report an aggressive, advanced, metastatic, high-grade, high-risk, or lethal incident prostate cancer endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Alcohol consumption showed no consistent association with prostate cancer risk, but a statistically significant inverse trend in risk for BPH.
estimate_classifications.reason: The alcohol association concerns overall prostate cancer risk, not an aggressive prostate cancer subtype.
